item.text: {"text":"HSTU combines content-based query–key scores with relative position/time biases before SiLU aggregation. Consequently, deletion effects cannot automatically be attributed to event content. For pure relative positional bias, deleting the latest event and compacting preserves distances among surviving events, but changes the readout event. Deleting an interior event reduces distances by one for surviving pairs spanning the deletion; distances within either side remain unchanged. These are architectural deductions, not published deletion-ablation findings. Timestamp handling also matters: Meta’s reference implementation uses a shifted next-event timestamp for each query, so deletion can change temporal biases even when retained event timestamps stay fixed. Absolute positional embeddings, if present in the supplied backbone, introduce additional shifts. [Meta HSTU implementation](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/hstu.py).\n\nRecommended frozen-model controls: compare compact deletion with deletion that masks the event’s attention participation while preserving original position IDs and the retained-pair bias submatrix; separately replace only item identity at the same position/timestamp using several matched replacement items. Keep candidate sets, padding width, normalization and evaluation users fixed. For interior deletions, retain the same final-event readout; latest-event deletion necessarily changes that anchor and should be reported separately. Read the final nonpadding position for left-padded histories. Bias-disabled or position-only/time-only inference can provide additional sensitivity checks, but introduces distribution shift and does not establish causal content importance. Report paired score/rank or validation HR@10 changes as intervention sensitivity. Published HSTU ablations establish that positional and temporal biases affect recommendation quality, but do not themselves separate these deletion confounds. [Relative-bias ablations](https://openreview.net/pdf?id=e6pqwHR1Yh)."}
